claims.text: The studied alloy has composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature BCC state.
Quenching from the high-temperature BCC state produces a sample with minimal pre-existing atomic order.
The quenched BCC state is metastable.
Sub-transformation-temperature annealing causes time- and temperature-dependent atomic ordering in the BCC matrix.
The annealing-induced ordered regions are incipient B2-like domains within the BCC lattice.
Ordered domains lower the local free energy.
Ordered domains act as preferential sites for secondary-phase nucleation.
Ordering-mediated secondary-phase nucleation produces a spectrum of phase transformations.
The extent and rate of ordering and the onset of secondary-phase nucleation depend strongly on annealing temperature and time.
At temperatures or durations that are too low, insufficient atomic mobility prevents significant ordering.
At temperatures or durations that are too high, thermal agitation, dissolution, or alternate transformations prevent the proposed ordering mechanism from operating.
Annealing near 600 °C for a sufficient hold time should produce ordering-related superlattice reflections in XRD or electron diffraction.
TEM should reveal ordered domains after annealing under optimal conditions.
Ordered domains should be absent from the as-quenched control.
Annealing outside the optimal ordering window should not produce significant ordering features.
Outside the optimal ordering window, phase evolution should resemble that of the as-quenched BCC state.
The as-quenched baseline has a purely BCC diffraction pattern with no superlattice reflections or ordered domains.

contradictions.description: The ordering window is described as specific but unknown and potentially requiring iterative calibration, yet failure to observe ordering only at 500, 600, and 700 °C for 1–100 hours is declared falsifying. A null result over those discrete conditions would not exclude an ordering window between or outside them.
